name: likwála
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Ikemou, Régina Patience. 2017. Elements of Phonology of the Likwála, Variety of Koyó Ngandza. International Journal of Language and Linguistics 4(3): 80-85. Center for Promoting Ideas, USA (ISSN 2374-8850). Publisher PDF:https://ijllnet.thebrpi.org/journals/Vol_4_No_3_September_2017/10.pdf
catalog_locator: p.85 (unnumbered tone section immediately before the Conclusion; p.6); abstract p.80
catalog_quote: Like the other Bantu C group languages, likwála is a tonal language. That is, it uses the variations of melodic high for lexical and grammatical. Tone is a supra segmental unit, it is as important as the segments. Tone is generally associated to vowels. likwála makes use of two tones, that is the high tone (H) and the low tone (L). These tones are susceptible to appear on any syllable. Examples: [image-only examples] The vowel of the extension suffix doesn't have tone. It receives its tone by the process of anticipatory association (Meussen, 1967) hereby represented. ... [Conclusion, p.85] At the prosodic level, this language only has open syllables. ... likwála uses two tones: the high tone and the low tone. Tones are steady in the lexicon as in the statement. ... [Abstract, p.80] likwála is a tonal language with two tones (High and Low) only.
world_status: statement found in an open source

The quoted passage is present verbatim at p.85, opening the (unnumbered) tone section directly before the Conclusion: 'Like the other Bantu C group languages, likwála is a tonal language. That is, it uses the variations of melodic high for lexical and grammatical. Tone is a supra segmental unit, it is as important as the segments. Tone is generally associated to vowels. likwála makes use of two tones, that is the high tone (H) and the low tone (L). These tones are susceptible to appear on any syllable.' The abstract sent…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Likwála is described as a two-tone (H/L) language with tones free to occur on any syllable; the description contains no statement about word stress or accent at all.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding prominence; only notes that the extension-suffix vowel is toneless and receives tone by anticipatory association (Meeussen 1967).
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical/grammatical tone on the word; 'Tones are steady in the lexicon as in the statement' (p.85 Conclusion). No phrase-level prominence discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Ikemou 2017 describes 'Likwála, variety of Koyó Ngandza' — i.e. Likwala (C26, likw1239) as spoken at Koyó-Ngandza in the Cuvette department east of Owando (per Ikemou & Nzete 2018); explicitly identified by the author as Guthrie C26 / mbochi group C20. Not to be confused with the separate Koyo language (C24, koyo1242), which the same author describes elsewhere (Ikemou 2018, LLA). Nzete 1983 concerns the Bokwele variety of Likwala.
